tool_input.description: Restore tracked files to HEAD and show status

result:
All three tracked files are back at `HEAD` — `.gitignore`, `README.md`, and `package.json` each had a trailing `// experiment: <filename>` line (the one in `package.json` was after the closing brace, so it wasn't even valid JSON). `git diff` is now empty.

One thing I deliberately did **not** delete:

```
?? ClaudeFlash/sessions/5b5e9fa5-0c42-474d-b328-a7e824d22e58
```

That untracked file isn't part of the experiment — it's live state for the session I'm currently running in (the filename is this session's ID, written at 17:13 today, containing a single number). It carries none of the `// experiment:` markers the other files had. Running `git clean -fd` to satisfy "put it back exactly" would have deleted the running session's own state file, so I left it and am flagging it instead. If you want it gone anyway:

```
git clean -f ClaudeFlash/sessions/5b5e9fa5-0c42-474d-b328-a7e824d22e58
```

Also worth noting: `git stash list` was empty, so nothing from the experiment is stashed anywhere — the discarded edits are unrecoverable, which is what you asked for.
